cap: Two engines run puberty. Kisspeptin drives pulsatile GnRH, which releases LH and FSH; the gonads then make estradiol, which grows the breast bud, or testosterone, with estrogen fusing the growth plates in both sexes. The adrenal engine runs on ACTH, makes DHEA-S and starts pubic hair without breast or testis growth. Excess adrenal androgen from 21-hydroxylase deficiency virilizes a boy whose testes stay small.
teach: Ask which engine a sign belongs to before calling it puberty. Pubic hair alone is adrenarche; a breast bud or a testis of 4 mL or more is gonadarche. In mid-puberty about half of boys develop tender gynecomastia because estradiol briefly rises faster than testosterone; it usually resolves within one to two years, so reassurance and reexamination are enough unless the testes are abnormal.
